key_insight: An explainable ML workflow combining SHAP/permutation importance with SR-KAN symbolic regression can discover closed-form inductance equations that generalize far better than standard black-box models.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, accurate self-inductance estimation for multilayer planar windings in high-frequency power converter design without relying on rigid hand-derived formulas.
method: Built an explainable ML pipeline using SHAP and permutation importance for feature attribution.
Applied Kolmogorov-Arnold Network-guided symbolic regression (SR-KAN) to derive analytical expressions with no prior structural assumptions.
Compared surrogate models against FEA simulations and validated the discovered equation on physical PCB prototypes.
evidence_signal: The study used over 10,000 FEA simulations across seven out-of-distribution classes and 55 PCB prototypes; the SR-KAN expression achieved 8.22% OOD relative error and 6.26% mean absolute relative error on hardware.
watch_item: The discovered equation is validated for the studied winding geometry and dataset, so performance may drop if the design space or operating conditions extend beyond the sampled domain.
paper_title: Explainable Machine Learning for Multilayer Planar Winding Inductance Estimation
